title: Evaluating Multimodal Large Language Model (LLM) (Generative Pre-trained Transformer 5 (GPT-5)) for Meniscal Tear Detection on Knee Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI): A Pilot Study

live_model.evidence: "Images were submitted to GPT-5 (model: gpt-5-2025-08-07) via OpenAI's application programming interface (API)" (Methods, Image analysis procedure)

prompt.location: Methods, 'Image analysis procedure': prompt quoted verbatim ('Analyze these knee MRI images ... Respond only with yes or no')
prompt.note: One call per case with sagittal T2 + coronal T1 PNG slices

data.source: MRNet validation set (Stanford, registration required); 100 of 120 cases chosen 50/50 with quality exclusion, case IDs not listed

notes: Reasoning-effort/verbosity settings not stated; 20-44 slices per series sent as 256x256 PNGs.

resolution.plan: Register for the MRNet dataset (Stanford AIMI) and use the 120-case validation set, or a seeded 50/50 draw of 100 cases with complete sagittal T2 and coronal T1 series; convert slices to 256x256 PNGs, send one request per case with the printed prompt to gpt-5-2025-08-07 and parse yes/no; compare accuracy with 0.76 (95% CI 0.668-0.833) at the set level.
resolution.approximation: The paper's 100 cases and its quality exclusions are not listed; reasoning effort, verbosity and service tier are defaults; the comparison is approximate and should fall inside the reported CI.
